study type: Retrospective cohort study with pre-post intervention comparison and contemporary control group comparison
outcome: Composite of postoperative mortality and multiorgan dysfunction
Delayed treatment (interval >6 months between recommendation and surgery)
Case mix of CHDs (complexity, neonatal surgery proportion)
cohort: The study included 11,895 pediatric patients (median age 2.0 years) with congenital heart disease (CHD) receiving treatment in low-resource regional hospitals or Shanghai Children's Medical Center in China.
finding: The interhospital partnership (ASSIST project) was associated with a reduction in delayed treatment, an increase in complex cases and neonatal surgeries in local hospitals, and resulted in equivalent primary outcomes (postoperative mortality and multiorgan dysfunction) between patients treated in post-ASSIST local hospitals and those in a major academic medical center.
